clinicalPearls: Preterm labour is regular uterine contractions with cervical change occurring before 37 completed weeks of gestation
It is the leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality, largely through complications of prematurity such as respiratory distress, intraventricular haemorrhage, and necrotising enterocolitis
The strongest predictors are a previous preterm birth and a short cervix on transvaginal ultrasound
Antenatal corticosteroids given to accelerate fetal lung maturation are among the most effective interventions to improve neonatal outcomes
Magnesium sulfate given before anticipated early preterm birth provides fetal neuroprotection, reducing the risk of cerebral palsy
Tocolytic drugs are used mainly to delay delivery briefly to allow steroids to act and to enable transfer to a unit with neonatal intensive care
Fetal fibronectin testing and cervical length measurement help identify women at genuinely high or low risk of imminent delivery
Group B streptococcus status guides intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis, and progesterone supplementation can reduce risk in selected high-risk women
reference.pathophysiology: Preterm labour is a syndrome with multiple pathways converging on premature activation of the mechanisms of labour: uterine contractility, cervical ripening, and decidual-membrane activation. Recognised triggers include intrauterine infection and inflammation, uteroplacental ischaemia or haemorrhage (decidual bleeding), excessive uterine distension (as in multiple pregnancy or polyhydramnios), cervical insufficiency, and maternal or fetal stress activating the corticotrophin-releasing hormone axis. These pathways generate prostaglandins and inflammatory mediators that stimulate contractions and cervical change ahead of term.
additionalDifferentials: Urinary tract infection or pyelonephritis provoking uterine irritability
Other causes of abdominal pain such as appendicitis
additionalInvestigations: Fetal fibronectin testing to help predict imminent delivery
Cardiotocography and tocography to assess contractions and fetal wellbeing
Speculum examination to assess for ruptured membranes and take genital tract swabs
Screening for infection including urinalysis and culture and group B streptococcus status
Ultrasound for fetal presentation, growth, and amniotic fluid volume
redFlags: Signs of chorioamnionitis such as maternal fever, uterine tenderness, and fetal tachycardia
Preterm prelabour rupture of membranes with cord prolapse risk
Vaginal bleeding suggesting abruption or praevia
Advanced cervical dilatation with imminent delivery at a very early gestation
reference.prognosis: Outcome depends heavily on gestational age at delivery; each additional week in utero at early gestations substantially improves survival and reduces disability. Antenatal steroids, magnesium neuroprotection, and delivery in a centre with neonatal intensive care improve results. Women with a prior spontaneous preterm birth remain at increased risk in subsequent pregnancies.
pitfalls: Mistaking true preterm labour for Braxton Hicks contractions and delaying steroids
Overtreating with tocolytics when there is a contraindication such as chorioamnionitis or significant abruption
Failing to give antenatal corticosteroids and magnesium neuroprotection within the appropriate window
Not arranging timely transfer to a unit with adequate neonatal facilities
Overlooking an underlying infection driving the labour
management: Give antenatal corticosteroids to accelerate foetal lung maturation and improve neonatal outcomes
Administer magnesium sulfate for foetal neuroprotection before anticipated early preterm birth
Use tocolysis (calcium-channel blocker or oxytocin-receptor antagonist) to delay delivery briefly to allow steroids to act and enable transfer
Arrange in-utero transfer to a unit with neonatal intensive care
Screen for and treat intrauterine and genital-tract infection and give intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis for group B streptococcus
Offer progesterone and consider cervical cerclage or pessary for those with a short cervix or prior preterm birth
Monitor the foetus with cardiotocography and plan mode and timing of delivery
Coordinate obstetric and neonatal teams and counsel parents on prematurity risks
